tasks.label: build
tasks.detail: Root gate `pnpm run build`: `prisma generate` for the demo app, then every workspace in topological order (`pnpm -r build`).

tasks.label: build: vscode-extension dependencies
tasks.detail: First step of `build: vscode-extension`: builds, in topological order, every workspace the extension depends on (`{./apps/vscode-extension}^...`: the eight packages and @debuggen/local-service), because the extension build reads their dist/ outputs — esbuild.mjs bundles the service from source against the packages' dist/ exports and copies packages/telemetry/dist/node/register.mjs — and a fresh `pnpm install` builds none of them. The filter is braced, because a bare directory filter with `^...` or `...` does not select dependencies, and strongly quoted so no shell rewrites the braces (PowerShell reads `{…}` as a script block). It is a task of its own so the extension's build keeps its unprefixed output: a run over several projects prefixes every line with `<dir> build: `, which the esbuild and vite problem matchers of `build: vscode-extension` do not match. Errors here stay in this terminal, and a failure stops the chain before the extension builds.

tasks.label: build: vscode-extension
tasks.detail: preLaunchTask of the "Run Extension" launch configuration and first step of `prepare: Extension + Service`. Runs `build: vscode-extension dependencies` first, so the extension's whole workspace dependency closure is built even on a fresh install, then builds the extension host (esbuild.mjs --production: dist/extension.js, the embedded service, prompts, schema and preload) and the webview (vite: dist/webview/main.{js,css}). Filters by directory because the extension's package name is `debug-generator`: `--filter @debuggen/vscode-extension` matches no project and exits 0 without building anything.

tasks.label: build: local-service
tasks.detail: tsup build of @debuggen/local-service to apps/local-service/dist/main.js, which `node dist/main.js` and the Playwright webServer run, preceded by its workspace dependency closure in topological order (the seven packages it imports through their dist/ exports, which a fresh `pnpm install` does not build). The filter is braced, because `./apps/local-service...` without braces selects the service alone, and strongly quoted so no shell rewrites the braces.

tasks.label: check: service port free
tasks.detail: Second step of `prepare: Extension + Service`. Exits 1 with an explanation when something already accepts TCP connections where the "Debug service" configuration binds: DEBUGGEN_HOST and DEBUGGEN_PORT (defaults 127.0.0.1 and 43117), read from the environment VS Code passes to both, then from apps/local-service/.env without overriding it, as the service's own dotenv load does. Such a listener would make the debugged service fail to bind while the extension talked to the other process; debug an already running service through the "Extension + attached service" compound instead. debuggen.serviceUrl must name the same address, as that setting's description requires. The script concatenates strings instead of using template literals, because VS Code reads a dollar sign followed by a brace in task arguments as one of its own variable references.
args: const TASK = 'check: service port free: '; try { process.loadEnvFile('.env'); } catch (error) { if (error.code !== 'ENOENT') { console.error(TASK + 'cannot read apps/local-service/.env, which the Debug service loads: ' + error.message); process.exit(1); } } const setting = (key) => { const value = (process.env[key] ?? '').trim(); return value === '' ? undefined : value; }; const host = (setting('DEBUGGEN_HOST') ?? '127.0.0.1').replace(/^\[(.*)\]$/, '$1'); const rawPort = setting('DEBUGGEN_PORT') ?? '43117'; const port = /^[+-]?\d+$/.test(rawPort) ? Number.parseInt(rawPort, 10) : Number.NaN; if (!(port >= 1 && port <= 65535)) { console.error(TASK + 'DEBUGGEN_PORT=' + rawPort + ' is not a fixed TCP port from 1 to 65535. The "Extension + Service" compound needs the fixed port that debuggen.serviceUrl names; unset DEBUGGEN_PORT for the default 43117.'); process.exit(1); } const address = (host.includes(':') ? '[' + host + ']' : host) + ':' + port; const socket = require('node:net').connect({ host, port }); socket.setTimeout(5000); socket.once('connect', () => { socket.destroy(); console.error(TASK + 'something already accepts connections on ' + address + ', where the "Debug service" configuration binds, so the debugged service could not start and the extension would talk to that listener instead. Stop it (a service started from a terminal or by pnpm dev, or the one the Debug Generator extension of another VS Code window started, which ends with that window), or start that service with --inspect and debug it through the "Extension + attached service" compound.'); process.exit(1); }); socket.once('timeout', () => { socket.destroy(); console.error(TASK + address + ' neither accepted nor refused a connection within 5 s, so whether the port is free cannot be told.'); process.exit(1); }); socket.once('error', (error) => { const codes = [error.code, ...(error.errors ?? []).map((cause) => cause.code)].filter(Boolean); if (codes.length > 0 && codes.every((code) => code === 'ECONNREFUSED')) { console.log(TASK + address + ' is free for the Debug service.'); process.exit(0); } console.error(TASK + 'cannot probe ' + address + ': ' + (codes.join(', ') || error.message)); process.exit(1); });

tasks.label: wait: service healthy
tasks.detail: preLaunchTask of the hidden "Run Extension (with Debug service)" configuration, which the "Extension + Service" compound starts beside "Debug service". Polls GET /health at the address `check: service port free` resolves until the Debug Generator service answers 200 with its health body (version, protocolVersion, pairingAvailable), so the extension activates against the debugged service and its debuggen.autoStartService probe never starts a second service on the same port. Fails after 120 s (DEBUGGEN_HEALTH_WAIT_TIMEOUT_MS, in milliseconds, overrides that bound for this task only); the "Debug service" terminal then shows why the service did not start. It concatenates strings for the same reason as `check: service port free`.
args: const TASK = 'wait: service healthy: '; try { process.loadEnvFile('.env'); } catch (error) { if (error.code !== 'ENOENT') { console.error(TASK + 'cannot read apps/local-service/.env, which the Debug service loads: ' + error.message); process.exit(1); } } const setting = (key) => { const value = (process.env[key] ?? '').trim(); return value === '' ? undefined : value; }; const host = (setting('DEBUGGEN_HOST') ?? '127.0.0.1').replace(/^\[(.*)\]$/, '$1'); const rawPort = setting('DEBUGGEN_PORT') ?? '43117'; const port = /^[+-]?\d+$/.test(rawPort) ? Number.parseInt(rawPort, 10) : Number.NaN; if (!(port >= 1 && port <= 65535)) { console.error(TASK + 'DEBUGGEN_PORT=' + rawPort + ' is not a fixed TCP port from 1 to 65535. The "Extension + Service" compound needs the fixed port that debuggen.serviceUrl names; unset DEBUGGEN_PORT for the default 43117.'); process.exit(1); } const rawTimeout = setting('DEBUGGEN_HEALTH_WAIT_TIMEOUT_MS') ?? '120000'; const timeoutMs = /^\d+$/.test(rawTimeout) ? Number.parseInt(rawTimeout, 10) : Number.NaN; if (!(Number.isSafeInteger(timeoutMs) && timeoutMs >= 1)) { console.error(TASK + 'DEBUGGEN_HEALTH_WAIT_TIMEOUT_MS=' + rawTimeout + ' is not a positive whole number of milliseconds.'); process.exit(1); } const url = 'http://' + (host.includes(':') ? '[' + host + ']' : host) + ':' + port + '/health'; const deadline = Date.now() + timeoutMs; let nextReport = Date.now() + 10000; let last = 'no answer yet'; const probe = () => fetch(url, { headers: { accept: 'application/json' }, signal: AbortSignal.timeout(Math.min(2000, timeoutMs)) }).then(async (response) => { if (response.status !== 200) { last = 'HTTP ' + response.status; await response.body?.cancel(); return false; } const body = await response.json(); if (body !== null && typeof body === 'object' && typeof body.version === 'string' && typeof body.protocolVersion === 'string' && body.protocolVersion !== '' && typeof body.pairingAvailable === 'boolean') { console.log(TASK + url + ' answered: Debug Generator service ' + body.version + ', protocol ' + body.protocolVersion + '.'); return true; } last = 'a body that is not the Debug Generator health response'; return false; }).catch((error) => { last = error?.cause?.code ?? error?.name ?? String(error); return false; }); const poll = () => probe().then((healthy) => { if (healthy) { process.exit(0); } const now = Date.now(); if (now >= deadline) { console.error(TASK + url + ' did not answer as the Debug Generator service within ' + timeoutMs + ' ms (last attempt: ' + last + '). The "Debug service" terminal shows why the service did not start.'); process.exit(1); } if (now >= nextReport) { nextReport = now + 10000; console.log(TASK + 'still waiting for ' + url + ' (last attempt: ' + last + ').'); } setTimeout(poll, Math.min(500, deadline - now)); }); console.log(TASK + 'waiting up to ' + timeoutMs + ' ms for ' + url + ' to answer.'); poll();

tasks.label: prepare: Extension + Service
tasks.detail: preLaunchTask of the "Extension + Service" compound, run once before either session starts: `build: vscode-extension` (the extension and its whole workspace dependency closure, which holds every package the tsx-run "Debug service" imports through dist/), then `check: service port free`. The first failure stops the compound before anything launches.

tasks.label: watch: extension host
tasks.detail: esbuild.mjs --watch for the extension host. Ready when esbuild.mjs prints `host built in N ms` (or `rebuilt` / `build failed` / `rebuild failed`). esbuild.mjs prints no per-rebuild start line, so a fixed rebuild error stays in Problems until this task restarts.

tasks.label: watch: webview
tasks.detail: vite build --watch for the webview. Each cycle starts at vite's `build started...` and ends at `built in N ms.` or `Build failed with N error(s):` (not at `watching for file changes...`, which vite prints before the first build).

tasks.label: watch: vscode-extension
tasks.detail: Starts `watch: extension host` and `watch: webview` in parallel and resolves once both have finished their first build.

tasks.label: typecheck
tasks.detail: Root gate `pnpm run typecheck`: `prisma generate`, then `tsc -b` over the solution tsconfig.json.

tasks.label: lint
tasks.detail: Root gate `pnpm run lint`: `eslint . --max-warnings 0` with ESLint's default stylish formatter.

tasks.label: format:check
tasks.detail: Root gate `pnpm run format:check`: `prettier --check .`. Each unformatted file is listed in Problems; fix with `pnpm format`.

tasks.label: test
tasks.detail: Root gate `pnpm run test`: `vitest run --coverage` over every Vitest project, including the guard-script tests.

tasks.label: test:integration
tasks.detail: Root gate `pnpm run test:integration`: the local-service-integration Vitest project (in-process service, deterministic provider).

tasks.label: test:vscode
tasks.detail: Extension-host suite (`vscode-test` via @vscode/test-cli, preceded by its pretest build). Needs a display; CI wraps it in `xvfb-run -a`.

tasks.label: test:browser
tasks.detail: Playwright `browser` project. Needs the built Chrome extension (apps/chrome-extension/dist) and the built local service.

tasks.label: test:e2e
tasks.detail: Playwright `e2e` project. Needs the built Chrome extension, the built local service and a migrated, seeded PostgreSQL (DATABASE_URL).

tasks.label: verify
tasks.detail: Aggregate gate `pnpm run verify`: build, typecheck, lint, format:check, test, test:integration and the three check:* guard scripts.

tasks.label: demo:db
tasks.detail: `docker compose up -d postgres`: starts the demo's PostgreSQL 18 container (the only service in docker-compose.yml).

tasks.label: demo:generate
tasks.detail: `prisma generate` for the demo app (writes apps/demo-app/src/generated/prisma; needs no database).

tasks.label: demo:migrate
tasks.detail: Checks the committed migrations, then `prisma migrate deploy` against DATABASE_URL.

tasks.label: demo:seed
tasks.detail: `prisma db seed`: loads the Lumen Supply catalog, warehouses, inventory movements and orders into DATABASE_URL.

tasks.label: demo: reset database
tasks.detail: Runs demo:db, demo:migrate and demo:seed in order, stopping at the first failing step (the order docs/DEMO.md uses).

tasks.label: demo:dev
tasks.detail: `next dev` for the demo app on http://localhost:3000 (or $PORT). Ready at Next.js's `✓ Ready in` line; compile errors (`⨯ ./path:line:col`) go to Problems.

tasks.label: demo:instrumented
tasks.detail: scripts/dev-instrumented.mjs: asks the running local service to launch the demo's dev server with the telemetry preload (POST /dev-server/launch). Needs the local service running (it writes the editor credential $DEBUGGEN_HOME/auth.json), the Debug Generator VS Code extension connected to it with this repository open (the service accepts that credential only for announced workspace folders), and packages/telemetry built so dist/node/register.mjs exists. Ready at `the service launched`. Stop it with Ctrl-C in its terminal (SIGINT asks the service to stop the dev server); Terminate Task hangs the terminal up (SIGHUP), which leaves that dev server running.

tasks.label: service: dev
tasks.detail: `tsx watch src/main.ts` for @debuggen/local-service (restarts on change; no inspector — use the "Debug service" launch configuration to debug). Ready when the service logs `the Debug Generator service is listening`. Stop it with Ctrl-C (SIGINT, which the service handles) rather than Terminate Task (SIGHUP, which it does not).

background.endsPattern: the Debug Generator service is listening|^debuggen: [A-Z_]+: |^Node\.js v\d+
